chapter: Earl Hines, Chicago and later gigs
title: Raymond Scott's band and Young's own bands on 52nd Street
summary: He played in Scott's studio band and led a band at the Yacht Club with John Malachi and Tommy Potter, another with Dexter Gordon, after Chicago's Capital Lounge.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I played with Raymond Scott in New York, Raymond Scott's band, the studio band. Charle Shavers was on that band.
When was that that you played with Raymond?
That's when I was working on 52nd Street.

I don't know. I'd have to go back and find that year when it was. But I had a little band at the Yacht Club on 52nd Street, and my piano player was John Malachi. My bass player was Tommy Potter. I got them out of Washington. And they went with Billy Eckstine later on, the
two of them with Billy Eckstine's big band. But I can't -- I couldn't tell you the year. I really couldn't tell you.
And I had another band on 52nd Street with Dexter Gordon playing tenor sax, and Jimmy Jones playing piano. Now, Jimmy could probably tell you the year that they were with me on that gig, see.

Yeah, I don't remember that date but I know it was on -- it was after I left Chicago with that little band that Tommy Potter because I played in Chicago with my little band at the -- this all happened after I left Lunceford. I played in Chicago at the Capital Lounge, right next door to the Chicago Theater. That Had a little lounge right on the corner there. I had a band.

Muggsy Spanier had the other band. We'd alternate there in Chicago. And I took that band right from there to New York to 52nd Street to the Yacht Club. Chick Goldman had the Yacht Club then. And the other band alternated with me in there was Lips Page. Lips had a nice band in there, and Sandy Williams was playing trombone with him in that band.
